title: Just 25% of Americans Plan to Dress Up for Halloween
paragraphs: For some Americans, fall is all about Halloween. For others, it's a time to enjoy good food and fun with family and friends.
But which fall activities are the most popular?
A YouGov survey in late September asked just over 1,000 American adults which fall activities they had already done or planned to do this year.
Watching scary movies was at the top of the list, with 47% saying they'd done this or planned to. Almost the same number said they'd enjoyed pumpkin-flavored foods or drinks, or planned to try some.
Halloween decorations were also popular, with more than four in 10 Americans having put them up, or planning to. Almost as many said they planned to hand out candy to children.
But although Halloween is a big part of fall in the US, some of the country's best-known Halloween traditions aren't as popular as you might think.
For example, only one in four Americans said they planned to dress up in a costume for Halloween. A similar number said they would carve a pumpkin.
About as many had already visited a pumpkin patch or planned to visit one. Pumpkin patches are places, often on farms, where people can choose pumpkins to take home.
And fewer than one in four said they planned to take children trick-or-treating or go to a Halloween party.

Other fall activities were even less popular. Just 13% said they would visit a haunted house, a Halloween attraction where people go for a good scare. The same number planned to go on a hayride, a traditional fall activity in which people ride around on a wagon filled with hay.
So while fall offers lots of ways to have fun, for many Americans, it seems a scary movie and a pumpkin-flavored treat may be enough to enjoy the season!
